title: The Uniform of the Cape Route
premise: In the winter of 1847, Ansel Underhill, a mapmaker's apprentice in the fog-bound port town of Cape Route, must complete the coastal atlas her dead master died protecting — an atlas whose true charts expose the smuggling route the town's victors have rewritten out of history. When the season's last bridge closes and the correction ship sails on the morning tide, Ansel has one winter to finish the maps, gather testimony from the fishermen and widows who remember, and get the truth notarized before the victors' historians burn the record. She ends by choosing found family over flight: she stays, publishes under her own name, and inherits both the shop and the town's memory.
about_author: Lior Eriksen is a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing chart corrections in northern port towns before turning to fiction. They write about the people history leaves off its maps.

chapters.title: The Last Correction
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ten years after her master's drowning, Ansel inks the final plate of his atlas alone in the map shop, hiding the true coastline beneath a false one as he taught her. Emotional beat: grief braided with complicity — she knows what she is erasing.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The harbor master announces the causeway bridge closes at week's end for the winter storms; anyone staying is staying until spring. Ansel hesitates at the toll gate, then turns back. Beat: the trap closing gently, almost kindly.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Widow Maren Kolve's POV. Maren brings her drowned husband's shipping ledger to the shop for appraisal, and Ansel recognizes entries matching the false charts. Beat: two keepers of silences recognizing each other across a counter.

chapters.title: Victors' Historians
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Alderman Voss arrives with a court historian to 'verify' the atlas before it ships to the capital, praising the master's posthumous loyalty. Ansel performs the obedient apprentice while noting which pages they measure twice. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Salt on the Vellum
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Working nights, Ansel finds her master's hidden marginalia — tide-marks that only make sense as a smuggling route the aldermen ran and then buried. Beat: the dead man speaking through ink; inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counts Waves
chapters.summary: Tobin, a harbor orphan's POV. Tobin watches Ansel burning papers late and starts leaving her found objects — a button, a coin — as silent blackmail or friendship, unclear even to him. Beat: loneliness seeking witness.

chapters.title: Maren Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren tells Ansel about the night her husband's boat was 'lost' — the same night the first corrected chart was signed. Beat: memory offered as a gift and a burden; Ansel accepts testimony for the first time.

chapters.title: A Map Is a Promise
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel begins drafting a second atlas in secret — the true coast — using Tobin as lookout and Maren's ledger as corroboration. Beat: cautious hope; the found family assembling without naming itself.

chapters.title: The Historian Stays
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The bridge closes early behind schedule; the historian, Calloway, is stranded too, lodging above the shop. He seems curious rather than cruel, asking questions no victor should ask. Beat: unease — an enemy who might be something else.

chapters.title: Ice on the Ink
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Calloway discovers a discrepancy between the atlas and his own survey notes and confronts Ansel obliquely over dinner. She lies; he lets the lie stand. Beat: a duel of courtesies, both aware of the blade beneath.

chapters.title: What Tobin Saw
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Tobin witnesses Voss's men searching the shop cellar and warns Ansel by the wave-counting signal they've invented. Beat: the child becomes guardian; stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: The Master's Grave
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the clifftop grave, Ansel admits aloud what she's avoided: her master didn't drown accidentally, and she has spent ten years surviving instead of telling. Beat: confession to the dead; resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Notarized in Winter
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel learns the truth can be entered into the record only if sworn before the sailing magistrate — who departs on the morning tide with the ship. A deadline is set. Beat: the clock made visible.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss offers Ansel the shop deed, legitimacy, and passage on the ship if she delivers the atlas uncorrected and forgets the ledger. Beat: temptation rendered generously; the reader sees why she might say yes.

chapters.title: The Night the Charts Burned
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Fire takes the harbor records office; Maren saves one armful of ledgers and shelters the group in her kitchen. Beat: loss hardening into solidarity — the found family becomes a conspiracy of witnesses.

chapters.title: Calloway's Choice
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Calloway reveals he was sent to bury the truth, not verify it, and shows Ansel his sealed orders. He offers her his testimony if she'll let him leave with clean hands. Beat: betrayal inverted into alliance, at a price.

chapters.title: Storm Work
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Racing the storm and Voss's men, Ansel finishes the true atlas plates while Tobin and Maren hold the door. Beat: craft as resistance; the climax's engine lit.

chapters.title: The Bridge in the Gale
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Voss moves to seize the plates the night before the tide; the group smuggles them across the closed bridge in the gale, Tobin nearly lost to the water. Beat: peak danger; the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Sworn Before Morning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the magistrate's lamp-lit chambers hours before departure, Ansel swears the true atlas, Maren's ledger, and Calloway's orders into the record as Voss pounds at the door. Beat: the climax — truth entering history by inches and signatures.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The ship sails carrying both atlases; Voss, exposed but unpunished yet, watches from the quay. Ansel chooses not to board. Beat: quiet triumph and renunciation — the record matters more than escape.

chapters.title: Her Name on the Plate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Spring comes; Ansel prints the corrected atlas under 'A. Underhill' and hangs the true chart where the false one hung. Voss's faction fractures as the record circulates. Beat: inheritance claimed openly.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, years later. Teaching Tobin — now her apprentice — the trade, Ansel teaches him which silences protect and which erase, and shows him the marginalia of everyone who helped. Beat: resolution; memory passed on as the truest map.
